title: Tensor injectivity from eventually split lifts on finite basis spans
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $M$ be a free $R$-module with a chosen basis $(e_b)_{b\in B}$, where $B$ may be empty or infinite [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and let $u:M\to N$ be an $R$-linear map. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set and $(F_i,t_{ij})_{i\le j}$ a system of $R$-modules, with $t_{ii}=1$ and $t_{jk}t_{ij}=t_{ik}$, whose compatible maps $q_i:F_i\to N$ exhibit $N$ as its colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For each finite subset $E\subset B$, write $P_E=\sum_{b\in E}Re_b$ and let $a_E:P_E\to M$ be inclusion. Assume that for every such $E$ there are $i_E\in I$ and an $R$-linear map $v_E:P_E\to F_{i_E}$ with $q_{i_E}v_E=ua_E$, and that for every $j\ge i_E$ there is an $R$-linear map $s_{E,j}:F_j\to P_E$ satisfying $s_{E,j}t_{i_Ej}v_E=1_{P_E}$. Then for every $R$-module $L$, the map $1_L\otimes u:L\otimes_RM\to L\otimes_RN$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The modules $F_i$ need not be free or flat, and the retractions need not commute with transitions or with changes of $E$.

proof.text: Fix an $R$-module $L$ and $x\in L\otimes_RM$ with $(1_L\otimes u)(x)=0$. By the tensor-product construction, write $x=\sum_{h=1}^n l_h\otimes m_h$ (absorb scalar coefficients into $l_h$). Each $m_h$ has finite basis support; let $E$ be the union of those supports and regard $m_h$ as $p_h\in P_E$. Then $y=\sum_h l_h\otimes p_h\in L\otimes_RP_E$ satisfies $(1_L\otimes a_E)(y)=x$. For $n=0$ take $E=\varnothing$ and $y=0$. Thus it suffices to prove $y=0$.

source.place: Tag 05FQ (lemma-universally-injective-local), proof: reduction to finitely generated direct summands; finite-support argument expanded using the basis and tensor-product definitions

proof.text: Tensor-colimit compatibility gives $N\otimes_RL=\varinjlim_i(F_i\otimes_RL)$ with maps $q_i\otimes1_L$. To put $L$ on the left, the bilinear map $(f,l)\mapsto l\otimes f$ induces the flip $F_i\otimes_RL\to L\otimes_RF_i$, and reversing the factors defines its inverse. Both composites are identity on pure tensors, which generate. The flips commute with every transition and $q_i$, since both composites send $f\otimes l$ to $l\otimes t_{ij}(f)$ or $l\otimes q_i(f)$. Hence $L\otimes_RN$ with maps $1_L\otimes q_i$ is the colimit of $(L\otimes_RF_i,1_L\otimes t_{ij})$.

source.place: Tag 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits); Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product) for the explicitly constructed natural flips

proof.text: Choose $i=i_E$ and $v=v_E$ from the hypothesis and set $z=(1_L\otimes v)(y)\in L\otimes_RF_i$. Functoriality gives $(1_L\otimes q_i)(z)=(1_L\otimes ua_E)(y)=(1_L\otimes u)(x)=0$. Apply filtered-colimit zero detection to the colimit in step 2. Since $I$ is small, nonempty and directed, it yields $j\ge i$ with $(1_L\otimes t_{ij})(z)=0$.

source.place: Tag 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit), applied to the tensor diagram supplied by Tag 00DD

proof.text: For this $j$ the hypothesis supplies $s=s_{E,j}$ with $st_{ij}v=1_{P_E}$. Tensor composition and identities therefore give $y=(1_L\otimes(st_{ij}v))(y)=(1_L\otimes s)(1_L\otimes t_{ij})(z)=0$, and consequently $x=(1_L\otimes a_E)(y)=0$. A linear map with zero kernel is injective: apply this result to the difference of any two elements with equal images. This works for every $L$ and uses only this individual $s$, with no flatness assumption on $L$ or the $F_i$.
